items.summary: Security disposition: evidence_needed. Keep new public exposure, go-live, and security-sensitive releases blocked. Permit ordinary reversible growth only when it introduces no new credentials, permissions, dependencies, data collection, or cross-site behavior. Evidence: the security baseline covers 61 sites, but fleet-doctor has no run or findings; operations deploy, uptime, and error sweeps have no results; authentication boundaries, secrets handling, runtime isolation, release controls, dependency provenance, monitoring, incident readiness, and security.txt/disclosure readiness remain unknown. Compliance reports 35 pass, 20 fail, and 6 unknown results. No compromise is evidenced, but missing telemetry is not clearance. Risk severity: high for public launch and security-sensitive releases; medium for bounded reversible growth. Exact decision: preserve existing private launch and release gates, continue authorized read-only evidence capture, and do not claim certification or a clean bill of health.

items.requested_action: Continue the existing read-only security evidence matrix using authorized metadata and retained artifacts only. Record dated evidence, affected scope, owners, severity, and release implications for authentication and access boundaries, secrets exposure, runtime isolation, release and deployment controls, TLS, dependency and supply-chain risk, data exposure, monitoring and incident signals, and security.txt or disclosure readiness. Do not retrieve credentials, access private containers, exploit targets, modify permissions or configuration, deploy, add dependencies, request duplicate telemetry, or conduct external outreach.
